newsitem.title: USA: Typhoon to reach Japan coast within 36 hours - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon to reach Japan coast within 36 hours - WSC.

text.p: Typhoon Opal is picking up speed as it tracks towards Japan and is now projected to make landfall along the southern coast of Honshu, east of Shikoku, in less than 36 hours, independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday.
Opal is likely to cause major damage to coastal property at and east of the landfall, with winds up to 120 mph and a storm surge of up to 25 feet, WSC said.
Strong wind gusts are also possible, especially to the east of the storm track.

As the system moves northward the winds will diminish but the very heavy to torrential rains will continue. Large areas of Honshu can expect rains of five to 15 inches, causing flooding and possible mudslides.
The typhoon will remain a major risk to shipping during the next 24 hours as it moves northward, bringing seas of more than 20 feet, winds up to 120 mph and heavy rains.
WSC said the system is currently located about 535 miles south-southwest of the southernmost point of Honshu and well to the east-southeast of Okinawa.
